gas.idealMaxDescription: Considered safe and optimal for minimizing work of breathing and physiological risks.
gas.hardMaxDescription: Absolute upper limit. Exceeding this significantly increases risk of CO2 retention, oxygen toxicity, inert gas narcosis, decompression illness, and immersion pulmonary edema.
gas.calculateGasVolume: Calculate gas volume and dive time for {{cylinder}}

gas.oxygenSafetyText: Gas blending with pure oxygen requires specialized training, oxygen-clean equipment, and proper safety procedures. High-pressure oxygen is extremely hazardous and can cause fires or explosions if handled improperly. Only qualified gas blenders should perform these operations.
gas.accountsForCompressibility: Accounts for gas compressibility at high pressure
gas.calculateOptimalMix: Calculate optimal gas mix for a target depth
gas.zFactorWhyMattersText: The Ideal Gas Law (PV=nRT) assumes gas molecules have no volume and no intermolecular forces. At dive cylinder pressures (200-300 bar), these assumptions break down.
gas.zFactorHowWorksText: Real gases compress less than ideal gases predict. A Z-factor of 0.85 means the gas only compresses to 85% of what ideal calculations predict.
gas.zFactorUsedText:
• Oxygen: ~0.87 at 200 bar
• Nitrogen: ~0.93 at 200 bar
• Helium: ~1.05 at 200 bar (actually expands slightly!)
gas.zFactorNistNote: This calculator uses NIST REFPROP v10 reference data with 2D inverse distance weighting interpolation for accurate real-gas calculations at pressures up to 300 bar.
gas.zFactorIntro: The Z-factor (compressibility factor) corrects for non-ideal gas behavior at high pressures.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: How do I log my first dive?
faq.a1: Go to the Dive Logs tab and tap the "+" button. You can manually enter dive details including depth, duration, water temperature, and conditions. If you have a Shearwater dive computer, you can also sync dives directly via Bluetooth.
faq.q2: Can I import my existing dive logs?
faq.a2: Yes! Erebus supports importing dive logs from UDDF files, Subsurface XML exports, and CSV files. Go to Dive Logs and look for the import option to upload your existing dive history.
faq.q3: How do I delete the sample data?
faq.a3: Sample dive logs and sites are added to help you explore the app. You can delete them individually by opening each item and using the delete option, or start fresh by going to your Profile and using the data management options.
faq.a4: Currently, Erebus supports Shearwater dive computers with firmware v93 or later. We use the UDS protocol for reliable data transfer. More dive computer brands will be added in future updates.
faq.q5: Why can't I connect to my dive computer?
faq.a5: Make sure Bluetooth is enabled on your device and your dive computer is in transfer mode. For Shearwater computers, ensure you have firmware v93 or later. Try restarting both devices and attempting the connection again. The app works best when your dive computer is already paired/bonded with your phone.
faq.q6: Do I need the native app for Bluetooth sync?
faq.a6: Yes, Bluetooth dive computer sync only works on the native iOS and Android apps. The web version does not support Bluetooth connectivity. Download Erebus from the App Store or Google Play to use this feature.
faq.q7: What decompression algorithms does Erebus use?
faq.a7: Erebus supports the full Bühlmann algorithm family: ZHL-16A, ZHL-16B, and ZHL-16C, all with configurable gradient factors (GF Low and GF High). We also support VPM-B (Variable Permeability Model) for bubble-based decompression planning.
faq.a8: Yes! The dive planner supports both Open Circuit (OC) and Closed Circuit Rebreather (CCR) configurations. For CCR, you can set your setpoint (PPO₂) and diluent gas mix.
faq.q9: How do I export my dive plan?
faq.a9: After creating a dive plan, you can export it as a PDF. This includes the dive profile chart, decompression schedule, gas requirements, and CNS/OTU tracking. Perfect for sharing with dive buddies or keeping as a record.
faq.q10: What is Real Gas Mode in the gas calculator?
faq.a10: Real Gas Mode uses NIST REFPROP v10 compressibility factors (Z-factors) for more accurate calculations at high pressures. This accounts for how real gases deviate from ideal gas behavior, especially important for high-pressure fills above 200 bar.
faq.q11: How do I calculate a trimix blend?
faq.a11: In the Gas Calculator, go to the Mix tab. Set your target mix (oxygen and helium percentages), your cylinder size, and target pressure. The calculator will show you the exact blending sequence.
faq.q12: How do I add my certification cards?
faq.a12: Go to the Certifications section and tap the "+" button. You can search for your certification agency and course, then take a photo of your card. The app will store your certification details and card image securely.
faq.a13: Gear profiles let you save complete equipment configurations for different types of diving. For example, you might have a "Tropical Travel" profile with a 3mm wetsuit and AL80 tank, and a "UK Wreck" profile with a drysuit and twinset.
faq.a14: All your dive data is securely stored in our cloud database with regular backups. Photos and documents are stored in encrypted cloud storage. We never share your personal data with third parties.
faq.q15: Can I export all my data?
faq.a15: Yes! Go to your Profile and use the "Export My Data" option. You can export your dive logs, sites, certifications, gear profiles, and more as an Excel spreadsheet, with an option to include your photos and videos as a ZIP archive.
faq.a16: Yes, your GPS coordinates for dive sites are stored securely and never shared publicly unless you mark your profile as searchable. Only your dive buddies can see shared trip locations.
